newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee shrugs off losses on the nearbys.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee shrugs off losses on the nearbys.

text.p: Nearby robusta coffee futures shrugged off early losses to end midday unchanged but other months were slightly lower in dull pre-holiday trading.
"The market is rather dead...we're in the Christmas mood already," said one.

Traders said players also turned cautious and were uncertain of New York's direction after the expiry of the December contract last night. Nearby months in London drifted off early and before bouncing back towards the morning close while volume was rather meagre and centred on nearby switches and crosses.
By midday, most-active March stood at $1,258 a tonne, the same as Tuesday's close, after touching a low of $1,246.
Turnover was 1,953 lots. Jan/March switch traded at $50-$55 while March/May saw deals from $35.
New York's December contract expired at 125.15 cents a lb, while the Dec/March switch, a barometer of spot availability, widened to 15.25 cents from 14.55 at the close on Monday.
Some traders said the previous December strength could spill over into March while others said the gradual stock build up on a seasonal supply rise could provide some downward pressure on March.
Traders said they would re-assess their position by mid-January when fresh supply data are released.
Technically, analysts said the market needs to muster support at the lows before attempting another rally towards $1,280 basis March.
"It's more likely at the moment that it's going to come down and test new lows," said Susan Rigg of Chart Analysis.
Traders kept a close watch on reports of a cold air mass which some forecasters said could cause freezing temperatures and possible damage to the Mexican coffee belt later this week.
"Frost is mostly likely on Thursday and Friday morning," broker GNI said.
"Mexico has suffered from frost before, alhtough the total quantity of coffee produced is around a fifth of that in Brazil," it said. "Veracruz, Puebla and Guerrero are the most vulnerable regions."
"However even the loss of half a million bags of coffee would be significant in the current market," the brokerage said.
